      "observations": [
        "The full31-path original patch adds same-account EWS MoveItem, ordered returned-ID mapping with an explicit version-driven syncRequired flag, local storage/header helpers, completion notifications, Rust bridge/request extraction, mock MoveItem/GetItem/sync state, one128-line move test and imported EWS serialization tests. All99769characters were read; third-party/generated checksum/dependency changes are functional context and not manual Thunderbird style examples.",
        "Original dispatch checks source/destination server object identity and isMove; same-server copies still stream through MessageCopyHandler. Fixed ExchangeFolder now handles same-server copy and move through CopyItemsOnSameServer, while cross-server traffic uses ExchangeMessageCopyHandler. FoldersOnSameServer still compares actual incoming-server objects, not hostnames. The EWS Rust request omits ReturnNewItemIds through Exchange2010 and requests it later; derived enum order and explicit RequiresResync carry this decision to the consumer.",
        "Both original and current local fast paths rely on response/input order, create corresponding local headers and write the new remote IDs. The explicit fallback flag replaces the rejected array-length heuristic. The original mock reuses the same IDs and original test asserts folder membership/counts; it does not independently validate distinct new IDs or every metadata field. The current move task also checks subject identity and global notification payload sizes. No server guarantee or real version compatibility was tested here.",
        "The review requests source and global-copy-service completion on success and failure. The author keeps same-server handling outside MessageCopyHandler and adds the local callback plus synchronous ScopeExit, explicitly reporting an rv!=NS_OK condition. That guard exists in the original landing. Current GuardCopyServiceExit uses NS_FAILED(rv) but still observes outer rv: the root-target return in CopyMessages occurs while rv remains NS_OK. The inspected message-copy service marks its source processed before dispatch and has no message-branch failure clear; NotifyCompletion is the consumer that clears and advances requests. This is a static captured-status/queue-validation gap, not a reproduced hang.",
        "The complete35-row review distinguishes an informational AttachHdr suggestion, the author reply saying it was changed, and the later ESR140compatibility objection. The actual final historical source and fixed LocalCopyMessages retain AddNewHdrToDB. LocalCreateHeader runs before offline copy, but insertion/commit follows the copy. The author hope that creating a header first provides a persisted recovery record is not established by this ordering or the detached-header contract. Existing lifecycle guidance is reused without rewriting it.",
        "The original helper distinguishes move/copy exclusion preferences and preserves selected flags. The fixed helper takes caller exclusions, always excludes storage/server identity properties and carries New/Read/HasRe explicitly; current LocalCopyMessages supplies dontPreserveOnCopy even when used by same-server moves. This is the actual current call path, not a claim that every original/server-only metadata field is preserved. ScopeExit releases after FinishNewMessage, so later header failure does not establish complete rollback.",
        "All original changed test/mock/serialization hunks were read. The original mock chooses Exchange2013 and directly invokes folder.copyMessages, then waits for local/remote counts. Current EWS/Graph move tasks await their shared global-copy helper, listener and notifications; the later Exchange2010 junk test provides bounded fallback-source coverage. Current copy tasks263–268 omit await/return for their async helper, and the later legacy test has zero-count assertions with two-message diagnostic strings. These are later static test gaps, not original-patch regressions or executed failures.",
        "Full primary Bug0–2 and D251633 creation-to-close timeline/all35actual rows were read. Ord comparison, direct ThinVec collection, documented callback inputs and personal Rust extraction were applied in the landing. Helper extraction was explicitly optional personal preference, not a new global rule. The protocol-agnostic comment retained an EWS-ID phrase in the actual landing despite a Done request; fixed comment later removes it. Good Try and build transactions are historical reports, not our test results. External docs, PRs and real servers were not opened or exercised."
